claim: Neural hormone oxytocin (Oxt) is produced by neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH).
source: Neural hormone oxytocin (Oxt) has received attention in this context because it is produced by neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH), a known output center of hypothalamic regulation of appetite.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The PVH is a known output center of hypothalamic regulation of appetite.
source: Neural hormone oxytocin (Oxt) has received attention in this context because it is produced by neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH), a known output center of hypothalamic regulation of appetite.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Oxt has an anorexigenic effect, as shown in human studies.

claim: Oxt can mediate satiety signals in rodents.

claim: Whole-body knockout (KO) of Oxt has little effect on food intake.

evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Acute conditional KO (cKO) of Oxt selectively in the adult PVH results in elevated levels of plasma triglyceride.

claim: cKO of Oxtr selectively in the posterior hypothalamic regions phenocopies hyperphagic obesity.

claim: cKO of Oxtr selectively in the arcuate hypothalamic nucleus phenocopies hyperphagic obesity.

claim: The arcuate hypothalamic nucleus is a primary center for appetite regulations.

claim: Oxt signaling in the arcuate nucleus suppresses excessive food intake.
source: Collectively, these data reveal that Oxt signaling in the arcuate nucleus suppresses excessive food intake.

claim: The body mass index of humans has increased dramatically over the last 40 years.
source: Understanding the neurobiological bases of appetite regulation is therefore an urgent issue, given that the body mass index of humans has increased dramatically over the last 40 years (NCD Risk Factor Collaboration, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to NCD Risk Factor Collaboration, 2016.

claim: Decades of studies in rodents have revealed molecular and neural circuit bases for body weight homeostasis.
source: Decades of studies in rodents have revealed molecular and neural circuit bases for body weight homeostasis (Andermann and Lowell, 2017; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Andermann and Lowell, 2017; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016.

claim: Classical studies with mechanical or electrical lesioning support the critical roles of appetite regulation by neurons in the arcuate hypothalamic nucleus (ARH).
source: Classical studies with mechanical or electrical lesioning, as well as recent molecular or genetic dissections, both support the critical roles of appetite regulation by neurons in the arcuate hypothalamic nucleus (ARH), in particular, those expressing orexigenic agouti-related protein (Agrp) and anorexigenic pre-opiomelanocortin (Pomc) (Choi et al., 1999; Ollmann et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Choi et al., 1999; Ollmann et al., 1997.

claim: Recent molecular or genetic dissections support the critical roles of appetite regulation by neurons in the arcuate hypothalamic nucleus (ARH).

claim: ARH neurons receive both direct humoral inputs and neural inputs of interoception to regulate food intake.
source: These neurons receive both direct humoral inputs and neural inputs of interoception (Bai et al., 2019) to regulate food intake antagonistically at various timescales (Krashes et al., 2014; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017).

claim: The paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH) is one of the critical output structures of the primary appetite-regulating ARH neurons.

claim: Silencing PVH neurons phenocopies the overeating effect observed in the activation of Agrp neurons.
source: Silencing PVH neurons phenocopies the overeating effect observed in the activation of Agrp neurons, whereas activating PVH neurons ameliorates the overeating caused by the acute activation of Agrp neurons (Atasoy et al., 2012; Garfield et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Atasoy et al., 2012; Garfield et al., 2015.

claim: Activating PVH neurons ameliorates the overeating caused by the acute activation of Agrp neurons.
source: Silencing PVH neurons phenocopies the overeating effect observed in the activation of Agrp neurons, whereas activating PVH neurons ameliorates the overeating caused by the acute activation of Agrp neurons (Atasoy et al., 2012; Garfield et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Atasoy et al., 2012; Garfield et al., 2015.

claim: Melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R)-expressing neurons in the PVH are the key target of ARH Agrp and Pomc neurons.
source: Melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R)-expressing neurons in the PVH are the key target of ARH Agrp and Pomc neurons.

claim: PVH MC4R neurons are activated by α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone provided by Pomc neurons.
source: PVH MC4R neurons are activated by α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone provided by Pomc neurons and inhibited by GABAergic Agrp neurons, and are supposed to transmit signals to the downstream target regions in the midbrain and pons (Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016.

claim: PVH MC4R neurons are inhibited by GABAergic Agrp neurons.
source: PVH MC4R neurons are activated by α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone provided by Pomc neurons and inhibited by GABAergic Agrp neurons, and are supposed to transmit signals to the downstream target regions in the midbrain and pons (Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016.

claim: The anorexigenic effect of Oxt has been shown in humans.
source: The anorexigenic effect of Oxt has been shown in humans (Lawson et al., 2015; Thienel et al., 2016), and genetic variations of Oxt receptor (Oxtr) have been implicated as a risk factor of overeating (Çatli et al., 2021; Davis et al., 2017).

claim: Genetic variations of Oxt receptor (Oxtr) have been implicated as a risk factor of overeating.

claim: Pons-projecting Oxt neurons have been shown to be active following leptin administration.

claim: Knockout (KO) and ablation studies question the importance of the Oxt-OxtR system in food intake and homeostasis of body weight.
source: Despite the importance of the Oxt-OxtR system in the food intake and homeostasis of body weight (Maejima et al., 2018), knockout (KO) and ablation studies still question such findings (Sutton et al., 2016; Worth and Luckman, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sutton et al., 2016; Worth and Luckman, 2021.

claim: Oxt or Oxtr KO mice showed increased body weight at around 4 months of age (termed late-onset obesity).
source: For example, Oxt or Oxtr KO mice showed increased body weight at around 4 months of age (termed late-onset obesity), while their food intake was not different from that of wild-type mice (Camerino, 2009; Takayanagi et al., 2008).

claim: The food intake of Oxt or Oxtr KO mice was not different from that of wild-type mice.

claim: Diphtheria toxin-based genetic ablation of Oxt-expressing cells in adult mice increased the body weight of male mice with a high-fat diet, but not those with normal chow.

claim: In diphtheria toxin-based genetic ablation of Oxt-expressing cells in adult mice, food intake was unaffected in both high-fat diet and normal chow conditions.

claim: Acute conditional KO (cKO) mouse models would be useful to revisit the function and sites of action of Oxt signaling in the regulation of feeding.

claim: The Oxt gene can be knocked out in adult mice using the cKO approach, avoiding the influence of possible developmental and genetic compensations.
source: Our approach offers the following two advantages over previous studies: (i) the Oxt gene can be knocked out in adult mice, avoiding the influence of possible developmental and genetic compensations (El-Brolosy et al., 2019); and (ii) the manipulation can be restricted to the brain, or even to a single hypothalamic nucleus, providing a resolution that exceeds previous studies.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the experimental approach, with a citation to El-Brolosy et al., 2019.

claim: The cKO manipulation can be restricted to the brain, or even to a single hypothalamic nucleus, providing a resolution that exceeds previous studies.
source: Our approach offers the following two advantages over previous studies: (i) the Oxt gene can be knocked out in adult mice, avoiding the influence of possible developmental and genetic compensations (El-Brolosy et al., 2019); and (ii) the manipulation can be restricted to the brain, or even to a single hypothalamic nucleus, providing a resolution that exceeds previous studies.

claim: Oxt cKO increases both body weight and food intake.

claim: The suppression of overeating and overweighting is predominantly regulated by Oxt neurons in the PVH.
source: The suppression of overeating and overweighting is predominantly regulated by Oxt neurons in the PVH, leaving Oxt neurons in the supraoptic nucleus (SO) with only a minor role.

claim: Oxt neurons in the supraoptic nucleus (SO) have only a minor role in the suppression of overeating and overweighting.
source: The suppression of overeating and overweighting is predominantly regulated by Oxt neurons in the PVH, leaving Oxt neurons in the supraoptic nucleus (SO) with only a minor role.

claim: In Oxtflox/flox mice, Cre expression deletes floxed exon 1 of the Oxt gene, resulting in the loss of transcription of Oxt mRNA.
source: To examine the necessity of Oxt for the regulation of food intake, we prepared recently validated Oxtflox/flox mice (Inada et al., 2022). In this line, Cre expression deletes floxed exon 1 of the Oxt gene, resulting in the loss of transcription of Oxt mRNA (Inada et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a description of the mouse model with a citation to Inada et al., 2022.

claim: The number of neurons expressing Oxt significantly decreased within 3 weeks after the AAV-Cre injection into the PVH.
source: Then, we injected AAV-Cre into the bilateral PVH of 8-week-old Oxtflox/– male mice (Figure 1A and B). The number of neurons expressing Oxt, visualized by in situ hybridization (ISH), significantly decreased within 3 weeks after the AAV-Cre injection (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The body weight of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection started to deviate from the controls at around 3 weeks after the injection.
source: The body weight of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection started to deviate from the controls at around 3 weeks after the injection (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: At 5 weeks after the injection, AAV-Cre-injected Oxtflox/– mice were heavier than wild-type (Oxt+/+), Oxt–/–, and Oxtflox/– mice that received vehicle injection.
source: At 5 weeks after the injection, we compared the body weight of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection with the wild-type (Oxt+/+), Oxt–/–, and Oxtflox/– mice that received vehicle injection. We found that AAV-Cre-injected Oxtflox/– mice were heavier than those in the other groups (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: The increase in body weight in AAV-Cre-injected Oxtflox/– mice was considered unlikely to be a reflection of late-onset obesity.
source: Importantly, this increase in body weight was considered unlikely to be a reflection of late-onset obesity, as previously reported (Camerino, 2009; Takayanagi et al., 2008), because we did not find a significant difference between the wild-type and Oxt–/– mice (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison with Oxt–/– mice and citations to Camerino, 2009; Takayanagi et al., 2008.

claim: Mice with a fewer number of remaining Oxt+ neurons showed a heavier body weight.
source: Next, we analyzed the relationship between the number of remaining Oxt+ neurons and body weight. We found that mice with a fewer number of remaining Oxt+ neurons showed a heavier body weight (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The daily food intake of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection was significantly larger at >4 weeks after the injection.
source: We also found an increase in food intake: the daily food intake of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection was significantly larger at >4 weeks after the injection (Figure 1H), and the total food intake during the 5 weeks after the injection was also larger in the mice that received AAV-Cre injection (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The total food intake during the 5 weeks after the injection was larger in Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection.
source: We also found an increase in food intake: the daily food intake of Oxtflox/– mice that received AAV-Cre injection was significantly larger at >4 weeks after the injection (Figure 1H), and the total food intake during the 5 weeks after the injection was also larger in the mice that received AAV-Cre injection (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The effects of PVH Oxt cKO are not due to the nonspecific toxicity of AAV-Cre injection per se.
source: Of note, these effects are not due to the nonspecific toxicity of AAV-Cre injection per se, as AAV-Cre injection to wild-type mice did not alter body weight or daily food intake (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by control experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: AAV-Cre injection to wild-type mice did not alter body weight or daily food intake.
source: Of note, these effects are not due to the nonspecific toxicity of AAV-Cre injection per se, as AAV-Cre injection to wild-type mice did not alter body weight or daily food intake (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by control experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Oxt neurons are clustered in the SO in addition to the PVH.
source: In addition to the PVH, Oxt neurons are also clustered in the SO (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The number of Oxt+ neurons in the SO significantly decreased at around 3 weeks after AAV-Cre injection.
source: To examine whether Oxt neurons in the SO also play inhibitory roles on body weight and food intake, we injected AAV-Cre into the bilateral SO of Oxtflox/– mice (Figure 2A and B). Similar to the PVH, the number of Oxt+ neurons in the SO significantly decreased at around 3 weeks after the injection (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Neither body weight nor food intake was significantly different in SO Oxt cKO mice compared with controls.
source: Unlike the PVH, however, neither body weight nor food intake was significantly different compared with controls (Figure 2D–G), and no clear relationship was found between the number of the remaining Oxt+ neurons and body weight (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D–G.

claim: No clear relationship was found between the number of the remaining Oxt+ neurons in the SO and body weight.
source: Unlike the PVH, however, neither body weight nor food intake was significantly different compared with controls (Figure 2D–G), and no clear relationship was found between the number of the remaining Oxt+ neurons and body weight (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PVH Oxt neurons predominantly regulate food intake and body weight, and SO Oxt neurons exert little influence.

claim: A significant increase was observed in the weight of the liver in Oxtflox/– mice with AAV-Cre injection into the PVH.
source: While the weight of the stomach was unchanged (Figure 3B), a significant increase was observed in the weight of the liver in Oxtflox/– mice with AAV-Cre injection, likely because of the accumulation of fat in the liver (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The increase in liver weight in PVH Oxt cKO mice is likely because of the accumulation of fat in the liver.
source: While the weight of the stomach was unchanged (Figure 3B), a significant increase was observed in the weight of the liver in Oxtflox/– mice with AAV-Cre injection, likely because of the accumulation of fat in the liver (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in liver weight.

claim: No significant differences in glucose levels were found in PVH Oxt cKO mice.

evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

source: In turn, the plasma concentrations of triglyceride and leptin were higher in Oxtflox/– mice that had received AAV-Cre injection than in those that had received vehicle injection (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A prominent increase in plasma leptin was reported in the late-onset obesity cases of 6-month-old Oxt KO mice.
source: Of note, a prominent increase in plasma leptin was also reported in the late-onset obesity cases of 6-month-old Oxt KO mice (Camerino, 2009).

claim: Intraperitoneal (ip) or intracerebroventricular injection of Oxt has been shown to reduce both body weight and food intake.

claim: Ip injection of Oxt (100 μL of 500 μM or 1 mM solution) once every 3 days significantly reduced body weight in PVH Oxt cKO mice at 5 weeks after AAV-Cre injection.
source: To examine this hypothesis, first, we injected AAV-Cre into the bilateral PVH of Oxtflox/– mice, and from the next day of the injection, we conducted ip injection of Oxt (100 μL of 500 μM or 1 mM solution) once every 3 days (Figure 4A). Ip injection of the vehicle was used as control. At 5 weeks after the injection of AAV-Cre, Oxt-treated mice showed significantly reduced body weight, even though the number of remaining Oxt+ neurons was not significantly different (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The number of remaining Oxt+ neurons was not significantly different between Oxt-treated and vehicle-treated PVH Oxt cKO mice.
source: At 5 weeks after the injection of AAV-Cre, Oxt-treated mice showed significantly reduced body weight, even though the number of remaining Oxt+ neurons was not significantly different (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Both daily food intake at 4–5 weeks and total food intake during the 5 weeks after the injection were significantly reduced in Oxt-treated PVH Oxt cKO mice.
source: We found that both daily food intake at 4–5 weeks and total food intake during the 5 weeks after the injection were also significantly reduced (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: The reduction of body weight and food intake by Oxt treatment paradigm was somehow specific to Oxt cKO mice.
source: The reduction of body weight and food intake by our Oxt treatment paradigm was somehow specific to Oxt cKO mice, given that neither reduction of food intake nor body weight was observed in wild-type males (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by control experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Neither reduction of food intake nor body weight was observed in wild-type males treated with ip injection of Oxt.
source: The reduction of body weight and food intake by our Oxt treatment paradigm was somehow specific to Oxt cKO mice, given that neither reduction of food intake nor body weight was observed in wild-type males (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by control experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Both plasma triglyceride and leptin tended to be reduced in Oxt-treated PVH Oxt cKO mice, but did not reach the level of statistical significance.
source: No significant improvement in the blood samples was found: both plasma triglyceride and leptin tended to be reduced in Oxt-treated mice, but did not reach the level of statistical significance (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: External administration of Oxt can rescue at least the hyperphagic obesity phenotype of Oxt cKO.
source: These results suggest that external administration of Oxt can rescue at least the hyperphagic obesity phenotype of Oxt cKO.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Oxt supplementation experiments.

claim: Previous studies showed that mice ate less within several hours after receiving ip injection of Oxt.
source: In addition to the daily food intake that we have examined so far, previous studies showed that mice ate less within several hours after receiving ip injection of Oxt (Arletti et al., 1989; Maejima et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Arletti et al., 1989; Maejima et al., 2011.

claim: Oxtflox/– mice that receive AAV-Cre injection show reduced hourly food intake after ip injection of Oxt.
source: To examine whether Oxtflox/– mice that receive AAV-Cre injection similarly show reduced hourly food intake, we measured food intake after 6 hr of fasting (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F). After fasting, the mice received an ip injection of Oxt, and food was provided again (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F). Cumulative food intake was measured at 1, 3, and 5 hr after the placement of food (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F). Although the number of remaining Oxt+ neurons was comparable (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G), Oxt-injected mice ate less (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Ip injection of Oxt appears to reduce food intake on the scale of hours to days, thereby preventing the hyperphagic obesity induced by Oxt cKO in the PVH.
source: Taken together, ip injection of Oxt appears to reduce food intake on the scale of hours to days, thereby preventing the hyperphagic obesity induced by Oxt cKO in the PVH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Oxt supplementation experiments.

claim: PVH Oxt neurons send dense projection to the hypothalamic nuclei.
source: Given that PVH Oxt neurons send dense projection to the hypothalamic nuclei (Yao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021), and that OxtR expression is also found in the hypothalamus (Fenselau et al., 2017; Mitre et al., 2016; Newmaster et al., 2020), we suspected that a fraction of appetite suppression signals is mediated by the other nuclei of the hypothalamus.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: OxtR expression is found in the hypothalamus.
source: Given that PVH Oxt neurons send dense projection to the hypothalamic nuclei (Yao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021), and that OxtR expression is also found in the hypothalamus (Fenselau et al., 2017; Mitre et al., 2016; Newmaster et al., 2020), we suspected that a fraction of appetite suppression signals is mediated by the other nuclei of the hypothalamus.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fenselau et al., 2017; Mitre et al., 2016; Newmaster et al., 2020.

claim: A fraction of appetite suppression signals is mediated by the other nuclei of the hypothalamus.
source: Given that PVH Oxt neurons send dense projection to the hypothalamic nuclei (Yao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2021), and that OxtR expression is also found in the hypothalamus (Fenselau et al., 2017; Mitre et al., 2016; Newmaster et al., 2020), we suspected that a fraction of appetite suppression signals is mediated by the other nuclei of the hypothalamus.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on prior knowledge and citations.

claim: AAV-Cre injection into the bilateral posterior hypothalamus successfully reduced the number of Oxtr+ cells in most of the targeted nuclei.
source: We found that AAV-Cre injection successfully reduced the number of Oxtr+ cells in most of the targeted nuclei (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Oxtr cKO in the posterior but not anterior hypothalamus significantly increased body weight.
source: Oxtr cKO in the posterior but not anterior hypothalamus significantly increased body weight (Figure 5I and J).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5I and J.

claim: A significant increase in food intake was observed in the mice that had received AAV-Cre injection into the posterior hypothalamus.
source: Similarly, a significant increase in food intake was observed in the mice that had received AAV-Cre injection into the posterior hypothalamus (Figure 5K and L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5K and L.

claim: Body weight, daily food intake, and cumulative food intake were significantly greater in the mice that received AAV-Cre injection into the ARH.
source: Body weight, daily food intake, and cumulative food intake were significantly greater in the mice that received AAV-Cre injection into the ARH, whereas no significant difference was found in the mice that expressed Cre in the LHA (Figure 6G-L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G-L.

claim: No significant difference in body weight, daily food intake, and cumulative food intake was found in the mice that expressed Cre in the LHA.
source: Body weight, daily food intake, and cumulative food intake were significantly greater in the mice that received AAV-Cre injection into the ARH, whereas no significant difference was found in the mice that expressed Cre in the LHA (Figure 6G-L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G-L.

claim: A fraction of the appetite suppression signals from Oxt neurons is mediated by Oxtr-expressing cells in the posterior hypothalamus, especially those in the ARH.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that a fraction of the appetite suppression signals from Oxt neurons is mediated by Oxtr-expressing cells in the posterior hypothalamus, especially those in the ARH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Oxtr cKO experiments.

claim: Oxt produced by PVH Oxt neurons contributes to the regulation of body weight and food intake.
source: In this study, we performed cKO of the Oxt gene by injecting AAV-Cre, which enabled region-specific KO of Oxt. By this advantage, we showed that Oxt produced by PVH Oxt neurons contributes to the regulation of body weight and food intake, whereas that by SO Oxt neurons does not (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Oxt produced by SO Oxt neurons does not contribute to the regulation of body weight and food intake.
source: In this study, we performed cKO of the Oxt gene by injecting AAV-Cre, which enabled region-specific KO of Oxt. By this advantage, we showed that Oxt produced by PVH Oxt neurons contributes to the regulation of body weight and food intake, whereas that by SO Oxt neurons does not (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The data extend the previous results that mechanical disruption of PVH in rats increased both body weight and food intake.
source: These data extend the previous results that mechanical disruption of PVH in rats increased both body weight and food intake (Shor-Posner et al., 1985; Sims and Lorden, 1986).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shor-Posner et al., 1985; Sims and Lorden, 1986.

claim: Whole-body Oxt KO mice showed a normal amount of food intake.
source: In contrast to the Oxt cKO phenotype (Figure 1H and I), whole-body Oxt KO mice showed a normal amount of food intake (Camerino, 2009), suggesting compensational mechanisms.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Camerino, 2009.

claim: The normal food intake in whole-body Oxt KO mice suggests compensational mechanisms.
source: In contrast to the Oxt cKO phenotype (Figure 1H and I), whole-body Oxt KO mice showed a normal amount of food intake (Camerino, 2009), suggesting compensational mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between cKO and whole-body KO phenotypes.

claim: When a certain gene is knocked out, expression of the related gene(s) is enhanced to compensate for some of the KO phenotypes functionally.
source: For example, when a certain gene is knocked out, expression of the related gene(s) is enhanced to compensate for some of the KO phenotypes functionally (El-Brolosy et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to El-Brolosy et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2019.

claim: Transcriptomic analysis between Oxt KO and wild type may reveal a more complete picture of gene expression that can explain the compensational mechanisms in Oxt KO mice.
source: Transcriptomic analysis between Oxt KO and wild type may reveal a more complete picture of gene expression that can explain the compensational mechanisms in Oxt KO mice.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: The phenotypic discrepancy between the current data and diphtheria toxin-induced ablation of Oxt cells might be due to the loss of Oxt cells outside the PVH that somehow elicited appetite suppression.
source: The phenotypic discrepancy between our data and diphtheria toxin-induced ablation of Oxt cells (Wu et al., 2012b) might be due to the loss of Oxt cells outside the PVH (maybe even outside the brain; Paiva et al., 2021) that somehow elicited appetite suppression, and therefore counterbalanced the overeating phenotype caused by the loss of Oxt in the PVH.
evidence: This is a speculation about the reasons for phenotypic differences, with citations to Wu et al., 2012b; Paiva et al., 2021.

claim: Neuropeptides or neurotransmitters other than Oxt expressed in the PVH Oxt neurons might have conveyed appetite-stimulating signals.
source: Alternatively, neuropeptides or neurotransmitters other than Oxt expressed in the PVH Oxt neurons might have conveyed appetite-stimulating signals, which remained intact in our Oxt-selective cKO model, but were disrupted in the cell-based ablation, resulting in only the overeating phenotype to appear in our case.
evidence: This is a speculation about alternative mechanisms.

claim: The data establish the necessity of Oxt in the PVH to suppress overeating.
source: Regardless of the scenario, our data establish the necessity of Oxt in the PVH to suppress overeating and suggest the presence of a hormone-based output pathway of PVH appetite regulation signals, in addition to the well-established neural pathways mediated by MC4R neurons (Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The data suggest the presence of a hormone-based output pathway of PVH appetite regulation signals, in addition to the well-established neural pathways mediated by MC4R neurons.
source: Regardless of the scenario, our data establish the necessity of Oxt in the PVH to suppress overeating and suggest the presence of a hormone-based output pathway of PVH appetite regulation signals, in addition to the well-established neural pathways mediated by MC4R neurons (Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, with citations to Garfield et al., 2015; Stachniak et al., 2014; Sutton et al., 2016.

claim: Several brain regions and cell types have been identified in the process of appetite suppression after eating a sufficient amount of food.
source: After eating a sufficient amount of food, animals stop eating owing to the appetite suppression signals mediated in the brain. Several brain regions and cell types, such as Pomc-expressing neurons in the ARH (Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016), glutamatergic Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH (Fenselau et al., 2017), and calcitonin gene-related peptide expressing neurons in the parabrachial nucleus (Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a), have been identified in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016; Fenselau et al., 2017; Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a.

claim: Pomc-expressing neurons in the ARH have been identified in the process of appetite suppression.
source: After eating a sufficient amount of food, animals stop eating owing to the appetite suppression signals mediated in the brain. Several brain regions and cell types, such as Pomc-expressing neurons in the ARH (Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016), glutamatergic Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH (Fenselau et al., 2017), and calcitonin gene-related peptide expressing neurons in the parabrachial nucleus (Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a), have been identified in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016.

claim: Glutamatergic Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH have been identified in the process of appetite suppression.
source: After eating a sufficient amount of food, animals stop eating owing to the appetite suppression signals mediated in the brain. Several brain regions and cell types, such as Pomc-expressing neurons in the ARH (Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016), glutamatergic Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH (Fenselau et al., 2017), and calcitonin gene-related peptide expressing neurons in the parabrachial nucleus (Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a), have been identified in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fenselau et al., 2017.

claim: Calcitonin gene-related peptide expressing neurons in the parabrachial nucleus have been identified in the process of appetite suppression.
source: After eating a sufficient amount of food, animals stop eating owing to the appetite suppression signals mediated in the brain. Several brain regions and cell types, such as Pomc-expressing neurons in the ARH (Ollmann et al., 1997; Sternson and Eiselt, 2017; Sutton et al., 2016), glutamatergic Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH (Fenselau et al., 2017), and calcitonin gene-related peptide expressing neurons in the parabrachial nucleus (Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a), have been identified in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Carter et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2012a.

claim: PVH Oxt neurons mediated appetite suppression signals.
source: Our data showed that PVH Oxt neurons mediated appetite suppression signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Both oxytocinergic neurites and Oxtr-expressing neurons can be found in various brain and spinal cord regions.
source: Previous studies have shown that both oxytocinergic neurites and Oxtr-expressing neurons can be found in various brain and spinal cord regions (Jurek and Neumann, 2018; Lefevre et al., 2021; Newmaster et al., 2020; Oti et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jurek and Neumann, 2018; Lefevre et al., 2021; Newmaster et al., 2020; Oti et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The data are generally consistent with the view that Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH evoke satiety signaling.
source: Our data are, therefore, generally consistent with the view that Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH evoke satiety signaling (Fenselau et al., 2017; Maejima et al., 2014); however, we do not exclude the possibility that OxtR in the other parts of the posterior hypothalamus, such as the VMH (Leng et al., 2008; Viskaitis et al., 2017) and medulla (Ong et al., 2017), also contributes to appetite suppression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, with citations to Fenselau et al., 2017; Maejima et al., 2014.

claim: OxtR in the VMH may also contribute to appetite suppression.
source: Our data are, therefore, generally consistent with the view that Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH evoke satiety signaling (Fenselau et al., 2017; Maejima et al., 2014); however, we do not exclude the possibility that OxtR in the other parts of the posterior hypothalamus, such as the VMH (Leng et al., 2008; Viskaitis et al., 2017) and medulla (Ong et al., 2017), also contributes to appetite suppression.
evidence: This is a speculation about other possible sites of action, with citations to Leng et al., 2008; Viskaitis et al., 2017.

claim: OxtR in the medulla may also contribute to appetite suppression.
source: Our data are, therefore, generally consistent with the view that Oxtr-expressing neurons in the ARH evoke satiety signaling (Fenselau et al., 2017; Maejima et al., 2014); however, we do not exclude the possibility that OxtR in the other parts of the posterior hypothalamus, such as the VMH (Leng et al., 2008; Viskaitis et al., 2017) and medulla (Ong et al., 2017), also contributes to appetite suppression.
evidence: This is a speculation about other possible sites of action, with a citation to Ong et al., 2017.

claim: One of the output pathways of the PVH for body weight homeostasis is mediated by Oxt signaling-based modulation of other hypothalamic appetite regulation systems.
source: Collectively, we suggest that one of the output pathways of the PVH for body weight homeostasis is mediated by Oxt signaling-based modulation of other hypothalamic appetite regulation systems.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: One possibility is that the primary hypothalamic neurons that are located outside the blood-brain barrier directly receive ip-injected Oxt and transmit appetite suppression signals.
source: Together with the importance of OxtR signaling in the ARH, one possibility is that the primary hypothalamic neurons that are located outside the blood-brain barrier (Yulyaningsih et al., 2017) directly receive ip-injected Oxt and transmit appetite suppression signals.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of Oxt action, with a citation to Yulyaningsih et al., 2017.

claim: OxtR-expressing neurons in the peripheral nervous system, such as those in the vagal sensory neurons transmitting intentional appetite suppression signals, may indirectly modify feeding.
source: Alternatively, OxtR-expressing neurons in the peripheral nervous system, such as those in the vagal sensory neurons transmitting intentional appetite suppression signals (Bai et al., 2019), may indirectly modify feeding.
evidence: This is a speculation about alternative mechanisms, with a citation to Bai et al., 2019.

claim: Future studies should further dissect the responsible cell types and physiological functions of OxtR signaling in the ARH.
source: Future studies should further dissect the responsible cell types and physiological functions of OxtR signaling in the ARH.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Recent advances in the real-time imaging of OxtR activities would be useful for delineating the circuit mechanism and spatiotemporal dynamics of the Oxt-mediated suppression of hyperphagic obesity.
source: Recent advances in the real-time imaging of OxtR activities, for example, with a circularly permuted green fluorescent protein binding to OxtR (Ino et al., 2022; Qian et al., 2022), would be useful for delineating the circuit mechanism and spatiotemporal dynamics of the Oxt-mediated suppression of hyperphagic obesity, such as by pinpointing the site of Oxt release.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions, with citations to Ino et al., 2022; Qian et al., 2022.
